title: The ratzon kadum in circles and in straightness: a will for Himself that holds every detail
overview:
Chapter 17 opens the details of the *Kav*, in circles and in *yosher*, by explaining the *ratzon kadum*. It is the simple will already decided in the Essence, come up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the Essence's own, yet its content is the same, and it is still a will for Himself: for His own sitting, not for the chair. Knowing Himself, He knows every detail, the way someone who knows a man knows his house. So every creature, a bug, a squirrel, a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect, and the finished house, the end of the seventh millennium, came up first.

The *Zohar* calls it *Atika d'Atikin* and *Atika Stima'a*; it is revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*. In the circles each lower level is only the will looking for a reason and proving it right, like a bribe. When the will is put into practice, the order turns over into *yosher*, with the deed outside. Of the *Ein Sof* itself nothing may be said; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*.

terms.gloss: the primordial will: the simple will come up in a thought, a copy whose content is the Essence's own, still a will for Himself

the hidden Ancient One: Keser of Adam Kadmon, already an Atik but still hidden
the holy Ancient One: Atik and Arich of Atzilus, the whole Keser, where the will and delight are revealed

the King's delight in Himself, before the tzimtzum, higher than Atika d'Atikin

a reason; there is no reason for a will, and the reason never reaches it
He engraved an engraving; the letters before the tzimtzum, still part of the mind, not a separate thought

sections.title: The Kav in circles and in straightness: the question the chapter opens
sections.summary: The chapter turns to the details of the *Kav*: it comes as an inner light, becomes a circle, and so on. The *Etz Chaim* says that in the circles the highest is the finest, and in *yosher* (straightness) the opposite.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum: the simple will come up in a thought, still for Himself
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is the same simple will that was already decided in the Essence, once it comes up in a thought. Its letters are a copy, no longer the letters of the Essence, yet its content is exactly the same; and it is still a will for His own enjoyment, not for the thing.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה ידוע שבחינת רצון קדום זה,
הגם שלגבי בחינת רצון הפשוט המוחלט בעצמות נקרא התפשטות רצון,
phrases.en: compared to the *Atzmus*, it's called *hispashtus ratzon*

phrases.he: אבל עדיין הוא בהעלם ולא בגלוי כלל
כי אינו רק השפעת והמשכת רצון הפשוט של חפץ חסד שהוחלט בעצמות מכבר, כך יהיה בפועל ממש
phrases.en: it is just simply the same *ratzon pashut* that was already decided, that that's the way it should be

phrases.he: ומיד שעולה במחשבה זאת שיהיה הכל,
phrases.en: and when it came up in an actual *machshava*

phrases.he: הוא הנקרא מחשבה ורצון קדום
phrases.en: that's what's called a *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: שכולל כל מה שבתוכו רצונות פרטים
כנזכר לעיל במשל הבנין

blocks.text: It is simply the same *ratzon hapashut* (simple will) that was already decided, that this is how it should be. When it comes up in an actual *machshava* (thought), that is called the *ratzon kadum*, the primordial will, which includes all the particular wills.
A *machshava* is a separate thing, in letters, as writing is separate from the *sechel* (intellect) itself. The only difference is that a *machshava* comes up, as it were, inside of himself.

blocks.question: Was the glif glifu (the engraving of letters before the tzimtzum) not also like that?
blocks.text: No. The *glif glifu* is not really a separate *machshava*; it is still part of the *sechel* itself, not an actual thought.

blocks.question: And what about the reshimu?
blocks.text: The *reshimu* (impression) is also the *glif glifu*, only the light of the *Atzmus* went out of it. But it is still how it was inside of Himself, so the *reshimu* is really considered still the *Atzmus*.

From the *reshimu* a line of *hispashtus* went out to the *ratzon kadum*, the *machshava kduma*. The letters of the *reshimu* were *mamash* those of the *glif glifu*, only without the light; the letters of the *machshava kduma* are different. That is why it is called *Atik*: a copy (*ha'atka*), no longer exactly the letters of the *Atzmus*. Still, it is the *machshava* of the *Atzmus*, as it is going to go to the outside; it is already coming out.

Compared to the *Atzmus* it is *mamash* a different thing: the *Atzmus* and its light are gone, as in the *reshimu*, and even the letters are not the original ones. Yet in its content it is exactly the same. Nothing really changed, even though it is only a copy.

So the primordial thought and will is *mamash* the same thing, including all the particular wills. Compared to the *Atzmus* it is called a spreading out of will, but it is still just for Himself, for His own enjoyment, not for the thing yet: "it's not really the chair, it's really his own sitting." That is the analogy of the building.

phrases.he: אם כן עדיין רצון קדום זה הכל בעצמו
phrases.en: It's really still all inside of Himself

phrases.he: בלתי התגלות לחוץ,
phrases.en: without coming to the outside, without being really revealed to the outside.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is really still all inside of Himself, without being revealed to the outside.

sections.title: Everything is made from it: knowing Himself, He knows every detail, down to the end
sections.summary: From the *ratzon kadum*, which is really Himself, everything is made afterwards, as from knowing a man you know his house. Every detail, down to a bug or a drunk in the street, is a detail of the King and deserves respect; and the end of the deed, the finished house, came up first of all.

phrases.he: אבל ממנו נעשה הכל אחר כך

blocks.text: But from it everything is made afterwards. This is the principle that by knowing Himself, He knows everything. How could He? The details were there, one may object, but not yet in the form in which they are made.

blocks.title: The size of his pants
blocks.text: The details are there. If you know a man, you know what size pants he needs: you know him, you have his measure. So here too, He is still not considered to know anything outside of Himself.

blocks.title: A house for a bird
blocks.text: As in the analogy of the building: here there is still no will for a swimming pool, only for swimming; not for a kitchen, but for eating; not for a bedroom, but for sleeping. If you know him, you know what bedroom he wants. If he is a bird, his bedroom will have a stick in it, and his house will have no stairs: you come in from the top floor. He is different, so the house is different. What he knows is not the house yet, but himself.
Everything is made afterwards from the way He is. That is not quite what it says: it says from this *ratzon kadum*; but in this *ratzon kadum* it is really Himself.

phrases.he: וזהו כי הוא אמר, במחשבה הקדומה,
phrases.en: He said in *machshava kduma*,

phrases.he: ויהי כו'
phrases.en: and then it was.

blocks.text: He said it in the *machshava kduma*, **and then it was.** As far as the *Aibershter* (G-d) is concerned, He said it there and was done; after that it came out by itself.

phrases.he: ונקרא חיי כל העולמים
מראש דאדם קדמון עד עקב אדם קדמון בסוף עשיה,
והיינו כל היצור לא נכחד כו'
phrases.en: that nothing is missing

phrases.he: שאין פרט היותר אחרון שלא קדם להיות ברצון ובמחשבה זו
phrases.en: There's nothing that wasn't originally over there.

blocks.text: "No creature is hidden" means **that nothing is missing**. In preparing the final thing, every detail of it has to come with a detail of the *Atzmus* it is being prepared for.

blocks.title: The king does not buy off the rack
blocks.text: We are talking about a king, and for a king everything is custom. He does not buy a suit off the rack, which the tailor then stretches here and takes in there, and even then the color is not *mamash* what you wanted. The same with the house. In us too, as will be said later, there is exactly what we want; we just cannot necessarily afford it. A king gets it: wine exactly as he wants it, "even if it costs a thousand dollars a bottle," clothes exactly as he wants them. So every little detail goes by a detail in the *machshava kduma*, which goes by Himself, and not one little thing is left out.

So the creature is very important here. Even a bug is somehow an enclothement of some detail upstairs. "No creature is hidden from You": there cannot be any creature that does not fit some detail upstairs.

blocks.question: What about the yucky things?
blocks.text: Even the yucky things are still yucky according to something upstairs.

blocks.title: The Atari game in the king's house
blocks.text: Even Amalek: how can it fit Him, when the whole thing is to kill him? Look at the guy's house. He has an Atari game, and it fights against him, and that fits something in his character. It *davka* has to fight him: "you don't want an Atari game that just says, 'Hi, how you doing?'" That fits the *midda* of *netzach* (victory).

So there is no little thing in the world that is not really it, not just an enclothement of it. It is *mamash* the *machshava kduma*, which is *mamash* the *Aibershter*: His stamp, and His stamp means it is *mamash* His name.

So you have to respect everything: "If you see a squirrel, you're seeing G-d." Anything that is in what He wanted fits some part of Him, as there is no part of the king's clothing that does not fit some part of the king: spit on any of it, even on the shoe, and you are spitting on the king. That is what "No creature is hidden from You" tells you: looking at anything, you are literally looking at the *Aibershter*.

No detail, even the very last, was not first in this will and thought: **There's nothing that wasn't originally over there.** So it doesn't matter. You see "some stupid dirty bum walking down the street half drunk" and say, "What about him?" Even the very last detail could not be there unless it was first over there.

phrases.he: ואדרבה
phrases.en: Just the opposite.

phrases.he: סוף מעשה, כמו בסוף אלף הז',
עלה במחשבה קדומה זו תחלה
phrases.en: It came up in this *machshava kduma*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות

blocks.text: Not only that: it is not that the worlds of *Atzilus* were *davka* there and we less so. **Just the opposite.** The end of the deed came up first in this *machshava kduma*. You see this in clothing too.

blocks.title: The outermost clothes
blocks.text: It is *davka* the most external clothes that represent the king. You can't go out into the street in your underwear: the inner clothes are not *mamash* the real honor; the ones on the total outside are.

blocks.title: The wallpaper, not the studs
blocks.text: The same with a house. What holds it up is the cement and the studs, the skeleton with wires and plumbing pipes all over. But what you *davka* wanted is the finished product, the wallpaper. He thought of a room surrounded with wallpaper; that drywall and studs have to be behind it is beside the point. When he planned it with his wife, "they didn't talk about the studs, they talked about wallpaper," carpet or parquet, and the ceiling was mainly the paint, not the drywall.

blocks.title: The chandelier and the decorators
blocks.text: He wanted to please his wife, and what she was thinking about was the fixtures on the ceiling, the beautiful chandelier: the most external level, done at the very end. First the studs, then the drywall, and for the construction crew it is a finished building. Then you walk in with the wife: "Look at this place. There is dust all over the floor, and it's not even a floor yet, it's just a piece of plywood!" Now come the decorators. And in the first thought, that is how you saw it, not the stuff behind it.

So here too the real thing is *davka* the finished whole, as at the end of the seventh millennium: even the physical world as it will be then, when we will have sat and studied *Shaar HaYichud* for a thousand years, with all its commentaries, like *Ayin Beis*. After the thousand years of *Moshiach* it is the thing He wanted, and then we can start on the fifty thousand jubilees. **It came up in this *machshava kduma*** first, as is written elsewhere at length.

sections.title: The Zohar's names: Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is *Atika d'Atikin*, the delight of all delights and the will of all wills, and *Atika Stima'a*, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*: still hidden, still for Himself. It is revealed in the *metzach* (forehead) of *Atika Kadisha*, *Atik* and *Arich* of *Atzilus*, where the will and delight for each world, and for each detail, come out.

phrases.he: (ובלשון הזהר נקרא עתיקא דעתיקין או עתיקא סתימאה
phrases.en: this *machshava kduma* is called *Atika d'Atikin* or *Atika Stima'a*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת רעוא דכל רעווין עילאין
phrases.en: it's also called the *ratzon* of all the *ratzonos*

phrases.he: דאתגליין במצחא דעתיקא קדישא כו'
phrases.en: these things are revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*

phrases.he: כי ברצון מלובש התענוג,
והיו לאחדים ממש
phrases.en: it's *mamash* one thing

blocks.text: In the *Zohar*'s language, **this *machshava kduma* is called *Atika d'Atikin* or *Atika Stima'a***: the *taanug* (delight) of all delights, the hidden delight. It is not yet a revealed delight, for the outside: "it's not a *taanug* for the chair, it's a *taanug* for himself to sit."

Besides the delight of all delights, **it's also called the *ratzon* of all the *ratzonos***, revealed in the *metzach* of *Atika Kadisha*. It has both names because the delight is dressed in the will and they become one: **it's *mamash* one thing**.

phrases.he: וברצון הפשוט ההיולי
שבחפץ חסד ההיולי (הנזכר לעיל באות יוד ואות יא)
היה כלול בו התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות
שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו כו'
וגם בג' מדריגות עד שבא בדבר פרט,
אנא אמלוך,
שזה בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני הצמצום
כמו שכתוב שם
הכל בחינת שעשועי המלך בעצמו בטהירו עילאה

blocks.text: The simple delight in the simple will, *sha'ashuei hamelech*, the King's delight in Himself, is *mamash* above *Atika d'Atikin*, which is already the actual delight. Over there it was still the *Atzmus*; not only not composite, but *hayah k'lo hayah* (as if it were not there). So in all three levels, *Yachid*, *Echad* and *Kadmon*, up to *Ana Emloch*, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*: all of it is the King's delight in Himself.

phrases.he: אך עתיקא דעתיקין מקור כל התענוגים
או רעוא דכל רעויין כו',
היינו בבחינת הקו שאחר הצמצום
שכולל כמה רצונות ותענוגים שעתידים לבוא בגלוי

blocks.text: *Atika d'Atikin* is the will for Himself, but in relation to the *Atzmus*: a preceding will for a house. But was it not said that this is not really a will for a house? It is not: it is a will for a home. A home is a will for oneself, but already in relation to a house.

So it is not like the *ratzon hapashut*, which is not a will for Himself but Himself; the simple delight is *mamash* Himself. This one is the will for Himself, which includes many wills and delights to come into revelation.

phrases.he: ועתיקא סתימאה הוא בבחינת כתר דאדם קדמון
שהוא בהעלם הרצון והתענוג לעצמו עדיין,
phrases.en: It's really still for Himself

phrases.he: רק שחושב להיות הדבר כך בפועל הגילוי
כמו להיות גילוי הרצון והתענוג להאציל עשר ספירות כו'
(ולכך נקרא עתיקא סתימאה בחינת העלם לגלוי על כל פנים
phrases.en: it's called *Atika Stima'a*: it's already an *Atik*, but it's *stum*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן ראשית הקו נקרא סתימא דכל סתימין
phrases.en: But the *reishis hakav* is called *stima d'chol stimin*,

phrases.he: דגם מחשבה דאדם קדמון לא תפיס ביה כו')
phrases.en: that even *Atika Stima'a* cannot grasp it

phrases.he: ולהיות הרצון והתענוג לברוא כו'

blocks.text: **It's really still for Himself**, only He thinks that the thing should be so in actual revelation: not just *mamash* Himself, but Himself "thinking in terms of sitting," so that there will have to be a chair, though He is not really thinking of a chair.

To reveal the will and delight to emanate ten *sefiros* is not really the will for *Atzilus* yet. **It's called *Atika Stima'a*: it's already an *Atik*, but it's *stum***. **But the *reishis hakav* is called *stima d'chol stimin*, that even *Atika Stima'a* cannot grasp it**. The sentence then skips the parenthesis: to reveal the will and delight to emanate, and to create.

phrases.he: ועתיקא קדישא הוא התענוג שבחכמה
והוא בחינת עתיק יומין ואריך אנפין דאצילות,
phrases.en: of *Atzilus*: what is usually called *Atik* and *Arich*

phrases.he: שהרצון והתענוג בא בגלוי
phrases.en: *Atik* and *Arich* is the *taanug* and *ratzon hagalui*; that's where the *gilui* is

phrases.he: כמו שיתבאר הכל דרך פרט)

blocks.question: What was said before, the will of all the upper wills revealed in the forehead of Atika Kadisha, seems to be a higher level than Atik and Arich of Atzilus?
blocks.text: *Atika Kadisha* is *Atik* and *Arich* **of *Atzilus*: what is usually called *Atik* and *Arich***. No, it is not higher. ***Atik* and *Arich* is the *taanug* and *ratzon hagalui*; that's where the *gilui* is**. *Raava d'chol Raavin* is the hidden *machshava kduma*, revealed in the *metzach* of *Atik*.

Even *Adam Kadmon* is called the hidden will: there is no revelation in it of what it is; that is only in *Atik*. Some places call *Arich* *Atika Kadisha*; here he explains it better: *Atika Kadisha* means the whole *Keser*.

The basic detail of *Atika Kadisha* is the *metzach*, the part of the *gulgoles* (skull) in front of the frontal lobe. A will comes into the brain, but the brain is hidden; the will is revealed in the *metzach* in front of it. We don't really notice it, but it is described in various places how the forehead lights up or gets sad.

blocks.title: Seeing through the hat
blocks.text: The big kabbalists can read your forehead. A man was told the *Rebbe* can see on your forehead what you are thinking, so he went with his hat pulled down. The *Rebbe* told him: "You think if I can see through your forehead, I can't see through your hat?" So the revelation of the will is in the forehead.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: *Atik* in *Arich* is the will and delight revealed: to emanate *Atzilus*, then to create, then for *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, to the end. As said last time, the will for *Atzilus* is the will to figure out in his own head what he really wants, a revealed will. So this is *Atika Stima'a*, and *Atika Kadisha* is the revealed *Atik*. In *Atzilus* he plans the house in his own head; in *Beriya* he goes to the architect, in *Yetzira* to the draftsman, and in *Asiya* to the contractor.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: So there is no detail that is not in there. The intermediary levels, though only conduits to the actual thing, have their own will and delight. In building a house, he sits with his wife and they plan what they want, and they get a big pleasure out of it, to the point that a person can enjoy the planning so much that he never gets around to doing anything. "This is called daydreaming."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: The rabbi and his gvir watch the yeshiva go up
blocks.text: While a new *yeshiva* building was going up, the rabbi would come with his big *gvir* (wealthy backer) and stand looking at it, plainly enjoying it, though it was only a building and others were building it. The pleasure was in the building stage itself, not only in the end product: it has its own delight and will.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.title: The artist's picture at the banquet
blocks.text: Even before that, at the first banquet, there was the architect's artist's representation of how the building would look. No building, not even the blueprint: just the picture, the concept. And there was a big delight even in that.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: There is a big delight even in shopping for a car, and especially in women one sees it: a big delight in the shopping itself, and before that in sitting around talking about what they plan to buy, above all when she is planning her house. There is a big delight just in that.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: So there is a delight in *Atzilus*, in *Beriya*, in *Yetzira* and in *Asiya*. But the biggest delight is *davka* in the end of the deed, at the end of the seventh millennium, when it is all accomplished.

blocks.question: How come he always says that we, now, are the biggest delight, even more than the end of the seventh millennium?
blocks.text: Where is there a bigger delight? *Chanuka* is coming up. Is it when the child graduates from *yeshiva*, or from college among the *goyim*, or when he is in the *Chanuka* play and you dress him up like a latke? Look at the parents at the graduating exercises, and look at the parents at the *Chanuka* play: the delight is bigger when he is dressed up like a latke. "And that's who we are, we're dressed up like a latke."
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.text: The *metzach* is the will. He reads it from the *Zohar* (*parshas Naso*): the forehead, which is called will, is the revelation of the whole head and skull. The skull is not the will; the *metzach* is the part of it you see, its revelation, and so the revelation of the will. The rest is covered by hair, and the forehead is in front, facing you. A person scratches his forehead; when he thinks, he looks up. One who knows can see all kinds of things on the forehead.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next class (the second side of the tape) goes on with *Atika Kadisha* and its *metzach* before it rereads lines 21-23; kept here, in class order, under the passage being discussed.

blocks.question: Where does this parenthesis start, and where does it end?
blocks.text: Rereading lines 21-23, the class asks whether a parenthesis should open before *Atika Kadisha*, closing at "in detail". The parenthesis that ends "even the thought of *Adam Kadmon* does not grasp it" opens and closes on its own. The one that closes at "in detail" opens far above, at "In the language of the *Zohar*" in line 14: this whole discussion has been one long parenthesis.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 026 rereads lines 21-23 in one breath (w1248-1279, aligned to line 21); the question is about the parenthesis that closes at the end of line 23.

blocks.text: That is the whole matter. The *ratzon kadum* is still a will for Himself, and it includes everything. It is *Atika d'Atikin*, the *Atik* of all the *Atiks*: of *Atzilus* (the will and delight to emanate), of *Beriya* (to create), of *Yetzira* and of *Asiya*. And of all the sub-*Atiks*: within *Atzilus*, *chachma* and *bina* of each level have a *Keser*, down to each detail of a detail. Every delight and will, to the last detail, is this delight and will.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23 and settles the parenthesis: the summing-up of what these lines say about *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.question: If everything is there for a delight, where do the yucky things come from, and why do they exist?
blocks.text: Even what is yucky is up there. A will has a positive and a negative: a *chazir* (pig), a repulsive thing, comes from a negative delight and will up there. Is a negative delight not simply pain, an absence of will? That is just what it is: a predisposition to hate this thing. Whatever has an existence has it because there is a delight for it; you hate and destroy it not because it exists, but because in the *machshava kduma* it was hateful. Then why does it exist? It is an Atari game: "It exists in order to blast it."
blocks.outOfPlace: Asked right after class 026 rereads lines 21-23, about their point that every detail's delight and will is included in *Atika d'Atikin*.

blocks.text: Like Amalek, the ultimate bad. Why does Amalek exist? Only so that there is the *mitzva* to kill Amalek. Since it is the opposite of the delight, there is a positive delight in getting rid of it, as two negatives make a positive. Why make it in the first place? Because there is more delight in destroying it. It is not that He hates it so much that He gets a delight in destroying it; that is just the point. We have no choice about bad things; we hope to get rid of them. But the one who made the world could have made it perfect; why make them at all? Look at the guy's house: his Atari game has weird creatures he has to battle and destroy, and there is a delight in destroying them. They were made for destruction.
blocks.outOfPlace: Continues the question on lines 21-23 asked right after class 026 rereads them.

sections.title: Circles one beneath the other: a will that bribes the mind to find it a reason
sections.summary: In the circles each cause surrounds its effect, and the effect never reaches it. A revealed will shows how: it comes first as one undivided will, and its *chachma* and *bina* are only a will to find it a reason and to prove the reason right, as in a bribe, or in politics. All of it is the will for Himself, down to the end of the deed, which is the innermost.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת עשר ספירות דעגולים זה תחת זה הוא כידוע,
שכל עילה מקפת לעלול
ועלול לא ישיג לעילה שלו כי אם בריחוק מקום ממנו,
כאשר יהיה האופן בתוך כו'

blocks.text: Until now he was talking about the *machshava kduma*; now he explains the circles and *yosher*: each circle surrounds the one within it, and the inner circle does not reach the one outside it, except at a distance of place from it.

phrases.he: ויובן זה מהרצון הבא בגלוי גמור
שגם שכלול הרצון הזה מי', חכמה ומדות,
phrases.en: Even though it has ten *sefiros*,

phrases.he: אבל תחלתו בא רק בהסכם א'
phrases.en: when it comes in the beginning, it just comes as one *heskem*, one *ratzon*

phrases.he: בלי התחלקות ניכר בו
והוא הנקרא עיגול רצון כללי
phrases.en: So even in a lower *ratzon*, *ratzon galui*, it first comes as an *igul klali*.

phrases.he: מקיף לכל מה שבא בתוכו מכחו דוקא,
אך בריחוק מקום

blocks.text: Now he makes an analogy from the revealed will. When you first have a will, it is just a will. **Even though it has ten *sefiros*, when it comes in the beginning, it just comes as one *heskem*, one *ratzon*.** **So even in a lower *ratzon*, *ratzon galui*, it first comes as an *igul klali*.** It surrounds all that comes within it.

phrases.he: כמו הטעם ושכל לרצון זה, שנקרא עלול שלו
אי אפשר שיהיה קרוב בערך אל עילתו, שהוא הרצון,
phrases.en: The *taam* cannot get close to the *ratzon*,

phrases.he: כי הרי אין טעם לרצון כלל כידוע,
phrases.en: because really there is no actual reason for a *ratzon*

phrases.he: ולעולם לא ישיגנו
phrases.en: it's not possible to understand it

phrases.he: אבל מכל מקום מכח הרצון נעשה עיגול החכמה גם כן
בלי התחלקות ניכר ליה כו'

blocks.text: **The *taam* cannot get close to the *ratzon*, because really there is no actual reason for a *ratzon***. It is not possible to understand it: a will has no *sechel*.
The circle of *chachma* is not actually *chachma*; it is a will of *chachma*: either the *chachma* to come up with a way to get what is willed, or a *chachma* to rationalize the will.

phrases.he: כמו משל השוחד, שימצא טעם לרצון
phrases.en: the *shochad* is that he should find a reason for the *ratzon*

blocks.title: The bribe
blocks.text: As in the analogy of the bribe: **the *shochad* is that he should find a reason for the *ratzon***. That is called rationalization.

blocks.question: Is this like chesed and gevura of Arich dressed in Abba, where chachma is a puppet for the will?
blocks.text: This is higher: not *Abba* yet, but the will itself, and in the will itself it is a bribe: he wants to come up with a reason. It is not actual *chachma* yet. Asked why he wants this thing, he wants to be able to give a reason, although really there is none.

phrases.he: וגם שבטעם זה כלול גם כן מיו''ד, רצון ושכל ומדות,
אבל נעשה בבחינת כללי כו'
ועל דרך זה לא ישיגנו העיגול דבינה שנעשה מכחו,
ועל דרך זה המדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה
שהוא עיגול האחרון

blocks.text: The reason has to include will, intellect and *middos*, but in a general way: it is just a will to have a reason for the will. So too the circle of *bina*: a will to come up with an analysis for the reason.

You find this in politics: a person wants something and comes up with a reason why, and a reason why his policy has to be correct. A guy wants to be president. Why does he want it? Because of this and because of that; he feels he can help the country. "It's not really true. He really wants to be president."

sensitivity.reason: Says that a man who runs for president only wants to be president and his reasons are not true.
sensitivity.publishable: You find this in public life too: a person wants something and comes up with a reason why, and a reason why his position has to be correct. Why does he want it? Because of this and because of that. But really he simply wants it.

blocks.text: Once they have a reason for a policy, they come up with a study, set up to prove it. In *yosher* a study could prove the thing was wrong. In the circles, the whole job of the *bina* is to prove the *chachma* right, and the whole job of the *chachma* is to prove there really was a reason for the will, that the will does make sense.

So too the *middos*, one after the other, down to the end of the deed. You see it in politics: it could be a man you can't stand, "but he's a Republican and you're a Republican, so you like him," just because he is a Republican.

phrases.he: והכל ברצונו לעצמו
phrases.en: It's only the *ratzon* for Himself still

phrases.he: כלול הכל עד סוף מעשה
שהוא הפנימי מכולם כו'
phrases.en: that's the innermost of all of them

blocks.text: None of this is actually *sechel* or *midda*: it is all the will itself, **the *ratzon* for Himself still**, down to the end of the deed, where He thinks inside of Himself how wonderful it would be to actually have such a thing happen: **that's the innermost of all of them**.

sections.title: The ratzon kadum is the daydream; doing it turns the order over into yosher
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* has the same ten circles, a dream of the end of the deed. When the will comes to be done, the order is reversed: the will hides in the intellect, the intellect in the *middos*, and the deed, the lowest, stands on the outside and on top.

phrases.he: וכך הוא ברצון הנעלם הנקרא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל,
מקור כל הרצונות
כלול מי׳ ספירות על דרך זה,
עיגול בתוך עיגול עד עיגול דסוף מעשה,
שהוא הרצון לסוף מעשה,
phrases.en: it's a *ratzon* for the *sof maaseh*

phrases.he: להיות כל אשר חפץ עושה בפועל ממש כו'
והעיגול העליון הכולל הכל הוא רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: As a revealed will comes, so it is in the hidden will called the *ratzon kadum*: all ten *sefiros*, circle within circle, down to the circle of the end of the deed. That is not a circle of deed; **it's a *ratzon* for the *sof maaseh***, that all He desires He does. "The whole thing is nothing but a daydream."

phrases.he: וכשבא הרצון לעצמו הזה להיות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: when it comes to actually being *b'poel mamash*

phrases.he: הרי הוא להיפוך
phrases.en: then it has to be the opposite:

blocks.text: So, **when it comes to actually being *b'poel mamash***, to have *yosher* you need circles first, because the circles are the daydream, the ambitions. Without the first will and all the wills inside it, down to the will for the deed, there is no *yosher*. The *Malchus* of the circles becomes the *Keser* of *yosher*.
At the end of the deed he sits around daydreaming how nice it would be. Then he says, "You know, but let's actually do it," and **then it has to be the opposite**.

phrases.he: שהרצון מתעלם ומתלבש בשכל
phrases.en: the *ratzon* has to be *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the *sechel*,

phrases.he: והשכל מקיפו

blocks.title: The kid who wants a bicycle
blocks.text: A man has a will for a house. Why? There is really no reason, but the will makes up a *sechel* so that he can give you one. A kid tells his father he wants a bicycle. Why? Because he wants a bicycle. Then comes the reason: he wants it so that he can ride to school, and do this and that. That is not really true.

Down to the will for the deed itself, he sits dreaming how nice a house will be, and in the daydream it is an infinite house, because that is how it is in the will. Then he decides to go and actually do it, and now he has to think: put the will aside and see what is really going on. How much money does he have? Can he really have such a house? The *sechel* takes over: **the *ratzon* has to be *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the *sechel***, and the intellect surrounds it.

phrases.he: והשכל מתעלם ומתלבש במדות זה תחת זה עד סוף מעשה,
phrases.en: And then the *sechel*, the *chachma*, has to be actually *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the actual, a real analysis of what's really going on here. And then it has to be *mislabesh* in the *middos*, *zu tachas zu ad sof maaseh*,

phrases.he: הוא העליון מהכל
phrases.en: That's the topmost.

phrases.he: דהיינו כח המעשה בפועל ממש
הרי בו מלובש המחשבה
phrases.en: In what a person does you can see what he's thinking,

phrases.he: ובמחשבה מלובש המדות
phrases.en: in what he's thinking you can see what his *middos* are.

phrases.he: ובמדות מלובש החכמה ובינה
ובחכמה מלובש הרצון והתענוג
ונמצא פנימי מכולם הוא הרצון והתענוג,
וחיצון שבכולם הוא המעשה
גרוע כו'
phrases.en: the lowest thing.

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת היושר כשבא בבחינת התלבשות העליון בתחתון כו'

blocks.text: **And then the *sechel*, the *chachma*, has to be actually *misalem* and *mislabesh* in the actual, a real analysis of what's really going on here.** Then it is dressed in the *middos*, one beneath the other, down to the end of the deed, which is above all.

**That's the topmost.** He made man *yashar* (straight): when you look at a person you see him in the way of *yosher*. What you see is the deed, the outside of everything, which stands on top. Inside his deed are his emotions; from what he does and says you can tell…

**In what a person does you can see what he's thinking, in what he's thinking you can see what his *middos* are**; in the *middos* are dressed *chachma* and *bina*, and in *chachma* the will and delight. So the innermost is the will and delight, and the outermost is the deed, **the lowest thing**. It is actually an enclothement: the will is actually dressed in the *sechel*.

sections.title: Why the ratzon kadum comes in circles and through a short line, and where speaking begins
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum*, still within Himself, comes in circles; to reach it from the *reshimu* takes a very great contraction, a short line. In the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, and one may not speak even of its *Malchus*; speech begins with *Adam Kadmon*. The *ratzon kadum* is His great Name, and it is not a new thing: it is part of the true *ayin*.

phrases.he: אבל בבחינת רצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל שעדיין הוא בעצמו,
phrases.en: the *ratzon kadum*: He's still inside of Himself, it didn't go to the outside yet;

phrases.he: על כן נמשך בבחינת עיגולים
phrases.en: therefore it comes in the way of *igulim*,

phrases.he: שהעליון מהכל הוא העלם הרצון הכולל הזה
ועיגול הראשון שבו הוא הרצון ותענוג לכללות כל השתלשלות שבתוכו,
ועיגול זה מקיף כללי לאבי''ע כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **The *ratzon kadum*: He's still inside of Himself, it didn't go to the outside yet; therefore it comes in the way of *igulim***, the uppermost of all being the hiddenness of this all-including will, and its first circle the general *makif* of *ABYA*.

phrases.he: וראשית הקו הוא בחינת המשכה היולית
כמו קו קצר המתצמצם מעילה לעלול,
כמו מן הרצון לחכמה
phrases.en: from the *ratzon* to *chachma* there's only a little thing goes through, not the whole thing goes through

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל
נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
מה שאין כן להיות רצון קדום שהוא בא לכלל השפעה חוץ מעולם האין סוף
רק שהוא היולי כולל הכל כו'
על כן נמשך דרך קו קצר כו'
ודי למבין

blocks.text: As **from the *ratzon* to *chachma* there's only a little thing goes through, not the whole thing goes through**, so from the *reshimu* a line is drawn in a very great contraction.

The *reshimu* is a limitation only in regard to the *Ein Sof*; to what comes after it, it is itself *Ein Sof*. So though you say the *reshimu* is nothing, to come down to the *ratzon kadum* you have to make a *tzimtzum* even from that: only a short line.

phrases.he: (והוא מה שכתוב בעץ חיים דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: The whole thing of the *Kav* is only to have up and down,

phrases.he: כמו ביו''ד עגולים עד סוף מעשה כו'
phrases.en: to make ten *igulim* one above the other till *sof maaseh*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בעולם האין סוף אין שם אפילו בחינת מעלה ומטה,
רק אחדות פשוט בתכלית כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: it's all one thing

phrases.he: וגם ששיער בעצמו מה שעתיד כו'
הכל הוא בעצמותו ממש שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש

blocks.text: **The whole thing of the *Kav* is only to have up and down, to make ten *igulim* one above the other till *sof maaseh***: an order of wills. In the world of the *Ein Sof*, the *reshimu* included, there is no up and down, not between *chachma* and *bina*, nor between *middos* and *sechel*: **it's all one thing**.

blocks.title: Knowing a man's taste
blocks.text: It is all in His very Essence, not a thing separate from the *Atzmus*. That He relates to a future deed is like taste: from a person's taste you can tell what he would like, but nothing is there other than the person. There is no actual separate will.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר בעץ חיים דגם בבחינת מלכות דאין סוף אין רשאים לדבר כו'
phrases.en: even *Malchus d'Ein Sof*, you're still not allowed to talk;

phrases.he: רק בבחינת הקו ובחינת אדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: you're only allowed by the *bechinas hakav*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת מקור הראשון לכל ההשתלשלות,
יוכל לבא בהשגה בריבוי ההשתלשלות עד עשר ספירות שבאצילות בבי''ע כו'
phrases.en: there you can come in *hasaga* with all kinds of *meshalim*, till you have the *mashal* of how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*

phrases.he: מאחר שנקרא בשם עילת כל העילות כו' או קדמון כו'

blocks.text: **Even *Malchus d'Ein Sof*, you're still not allowed to talk**, because there is nothing to talk about: there is no separate thing to speak of.

**You're only allowed by the *bechinas hakav***, from *Adam Kadmon*. Even the beginning of the *Kav* is *stima d'chol stimin*, which no thought grasps. From *Adam Kadmon* you may start: **there you can come in *hasaga* with all kinds of *meshalim***, down to *Atzilus* in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and to how they are in us. *Kadmon* here means *Adam Kadmon*, not the *Kadmon* before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: אבל בעצמות אור אין סוף לית מחשבה תפיסא ביה, אפילו מחשבה הקדומה הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: even the *machshava kduma* cannot grasp in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*,

phrases.he: להיות כי העולם האין סוף נבדל בערך ונקרא קדוש לגמרי מצד הצמצום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: because the *helem* of the *Ein Sof* totally has nothing to do with after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ובחינת רצון קדום הנזכר לעיל נקרא שמו הגדול,
שמו גימטריא רצון,
והוא ענין יהא שמיה רבה מברך כו'

blocks.text: There, in the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof*, even the *machshava kduma* cannot grasp. The hidden *Ein Sof* has totally nothing to do with what is after the *tzimtzum*.

"May His great Name be blessed": the great Name, the upper general will, the original *machshava kduma* for the end of the deed of the seventh millennium, should come down to here: *Moshiach* should come.

phrases.he: (וכידוע דבחינת אדם קדמון נקרא אדם דבריאה כו'
וכמו שיתבאר
מה שאין כן בעצמות אור אין סוף נאמר כי לא אדם הוא כו'
phrases.en: In *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* it says He's not a man.

phrases.he: וכידוע בכונות דנשמת כל חי, שהוא בחינת אדם קדמון כו'
ודי למבין):

blocks.text: **In *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* it says He's not a man.** *Adam Kadmon* is called a man: it already has the shape of a man. In the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* there is no shape at all. With this the chapter ends.

After the chapter he adds: sometimes he wants commerce and sometimes not; that is the will for himself, which causes the will for a will. He wants to be himself and have all he needs, so it makes a will to have a will for anything he needs to be himself.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end ("And that was chapter 17"), on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

blocks.text: So the *ratzon kadum* is not a new creation. It was always there, part of the true *ayin* (nothing). *Ayin* does not mean a nothing, for a nothing could not have made the something; it means not a something by itself. The *ratzon kadum* is literally part of Him, not a separate entity.
blocks.outOfPlace: Said after the chapter is read to the end, on the ratzon kadum of the whole chapter.

reviewQuestions.question: How does the ratzon kadum differ from the ratzon hapashut, and in what way is it still the same thing?
How can the ratzon kadum hold every detail when it is only a will for Himself? What do the bird's house and the king's suit show?
Why did the end of the deed come up first in the primordial thought?
What are Atika d'Atikin, Atika Stima'a and Atika Kadisha, and where is the will revealed?
In the circles, what are chachma and bina to the will, and why does the effect never reach its cause?
Why is the order reversed in yosher, so that the deed is the uppermost and the will the innermost?

notes.text: Class 025 is catalogued as "Ch16" (Tape023-Side1-Ch16) but reads chapter 17 from its first word, lines 1-23.
Line 62 is marked NOT READ by the alignment, but class 027 reads it at w802-813 ("ki yadua b'kavanos d'Nishmas kol chai..."); it is cited in the passage of lines 60-62.

Class 026 opens by going back to the metzach of Atika Kadisha and the Atiks of each world, and only at w1248 rereads lines 21-23; all of w0-2215 is kept, in class order, under the passage of lines 22-23 with outOfPlace. The latke question (w837-1031) and the keyPoint before it are about the end of the deed of line 13.
025 w3339-3420: the transcript has no speakers, and it is unclear whether "I read in some places that Atika Kadisha is Arich" is Rabbi Markel or the student; the block says it impersonally.

026 w1060-1075: he reads the Zohar (parshas Naso, as the student says) on the metzach; the transcript's Hebrew is rough. The block gives only what he explains (the forehead, called will, is the revelation of the whole head and skull) and leaves out the rest of the quotation ("covered in four hundred and twenty worlds" as transcribed).

027 w819-879, after "And that was chapter 17": the transcript has "sometimes he wants mischar (trade) and sometimes he doesn't"; the word may be misheard, so the block leaves it out. The recording jumps from 6:20 to 6:30 just before it, and this may be the start of a further discussion.
The story of the man who wore his hat down to the Rebbe who reads foreheads: he does not say which Rebbe.
In reading line 3 he says "ha'elyon gavoha" for ha'elyon garua, and in line 24 the transcript has igul for ila; the phrases follow the chapter text.

A phrase's English is only Rabbi Markel's own rendering in class, anchored to where he says it; where he only reads the Hebrew (lines 1-3, 16-18, 24 and most of 41-62) or only explains it, the phrase has no English.
"That's why it's called Atik. It's a copy of those letters": he reads Atik as ha'atka, a copy (chapter 16's spelling).
Class 026 has Sofer's word times, not re-timed ones; its seconds may be off.
027 w670-683: he reads ha'olam ha'Ein Sof as he'elem ha'Ein Sof, and his English keeps it ("the helem of the Ein Sof"); the phrase's English follows what he says.

025 w3228-3249: with no speakers in the transcript, "Atika Kadisha is Atik and Arich... of Atzilus, means what is usually called Atik and Arich" may be partly the student's; it is taken as the class's rendering of line 23.
